summary: The board-specific logic in rtl/dottori.v is a gate-and-counter netlist of the small TTL board. It has four cascaded 4-bit counters named after the IC positions, raw carry chains, sync and blank built from counter-bit gates, and a 157-style mux that hands the RAM address to either the Z80 or the raster counters. A 166-style shift register serializes pixels, and the Z80's clock is gated during VRAM fetch. None of MAME's decomposition carries over: MAME uses screen_update with a per-pixel loop, vram_w/color_w handlers, and scanline timers that rescale the CPU clock to 0.75x.

findings.note: The H/V timing comes from four 4-bit counters (COUNT_IC10..IC13), linked by explicit CARRY_A/B/C terms. IC12/IC13 are clocked by a counter bit (posedge n4M_128), not by a single system clock, the way a 74161 cascade is wired. MAME only declares raw screen parameters.

findings.signal: Raster counter bits as RAM address
findings.note: During the fetch phase, the RAM address is a direct concatenation of counter bits through a 157-style mux (nLD select). MAME instead computes the index arithmetically as x>>3 | y>>1<<4.
SHIFT_REG loads on nLD and shifts out MSB-first on every pixel clock, as an LS166 does. MAME reads a latched byte bit by bit with (latch >> (~x & 7)) & 1.

findings.signal: CPU clock gating for VRAM contention
findings.note: The Z80 clock is stopped (CLK_Z80 = CLK_4M | nVRAMWREN) by a flip-flop that a counter-decoded term drives, so the stall falls on the real fetch cycles. MAME approximates this by setting the CPU clock to 0.75x for part of each line.
H-sync, V-sync, composite sync and blanking come from NAND/NOR/AND combinations of specific counter outputs (LS10_12, IC4_1, IC4_4, LS08_6), written as individual gate outputs.
nINT is a flip-flop that the line counter's carry-out (CARRY_C) samples. MAME schedules a timer pulse at scanline 191, hpos 192.
The color register is a 174-style latch clocked on the rising edge of the decoded /IOWR (nWR|nIORQ), with no port-address decode, rather than a write-handler function.
Identifiers name chip outputs and counter taps (IC10_14, IC16_11, LS10_12, n4M_4096, CLK_4M_32768) instead of semantic names such as hcount or vcount.

Memory and IO decode is built from active-low strobes and A15 only (nRAM_WR = NAND of A15, VRAMWREN, MREQ/WR), and RAM is mirrored across 8000-FFFF by its 11 address bits. The decode is not shaped like MAME's region map.
The MiSTer wrapper, the TV80 Z80 wrapper and the generic BRAM modules carry no board-specific evidence.
